basis: Systemic hypersensitivity; airway compromise and circulatory failure are major diagnostic criteria. Transient rash and gastrointestinal symptoms do not establish additional organ damage.

decisions.cardiovascular: primary: hypotension/circulatory failure is a major anaphylaxis diagnostic criterion, rather than evidence of a separate cardiac disease.
decisions.pulmonary: primary: acute airway edema and bronchospasm with respiratory compromise are major diagnostic criteria.

basis: Neurodevelopmental impairment affects most classic cases; microcephaly 80-99%. Cap omits ichthyosis/dental defects 80-99%; severe intellectual disability alone is annotated 5-29%.

decisions.neurologic: involved: developmental impairment is typical and microcephaly occurs in 80-99%; the 5-29% annotation concerns severe intellectual disability, not all neurologic impairment.
decisions.dermatologic: none under cap: ichthyosis occurs in 80-99%, but defining metabolic, skeletal and ocular disease plus disabling neurologic involvement take priority.

basis: Inherited spastic paraplegia; visual loss occurs in 30-79%. Bladder and bowel control abnormalities lack evidence of direct urinary or intestinal disease.

decisions.ocular: involved: visual loss is annotated in 30-79%, supporting substantial visual functional impairment; nystagmus alone would not suffice.

basis: Predominantly CNS tumor; supplied HPO reports retinal capillary tumors in 80-99%, supporting ocular occupation. Neurogenic bladder/bowel findings do not establish direct visceral damage.

decisions.ocular: involved: supplied retinal capillary hemangioma frequency is 80-99%; direct tumor occupation meets the rule despite uncertainty about this broad annotation.

basis: SELENON skeletal myopathy; reduced vital capacity 14/14 and hypoventilation 10/17 arise from respiratory muscle weakness and spinal restriction, without direct lung or airway disease.

decisions.pulmonary: none: frequent ventilatory failure reflects diseased respiratory skeletal muscles and chest restriction; direct pulmonary tissue or airway involvement is not established.

basis: Defining vascular, metabolic and neurologic disease; progressive nephropathy 30-79%. Cap prioritizes renal severity over deafness/anemia 80-99% and skeletal abnormalities 30-79%.

decisions.renal: involved: progressive nephropathy/nephrotic syndrome occurs in 30-79% and is a defining feature; potentially severe renal failure merits the fourth axis.
decisions.otologic: none under cap: sensorineural deafness occurs in 80-99%, but severe progressive renal disease is prioritized after the three defining primary axes.

basis: Inherited peripheral neuropathy; persistent distal muscle atrophy and fixed foot deformities affect most patients, representing structural tissue loss beyond weakness alone.

decisions.musculoskeletal: involved: chronic distal muscle wasting and fixed foot deformities affect most patients; established tissue loss and deformity qualify beyond transient weakness.

basis: Immune/blood-cell defects and ocular albinism define CHS; neurologic decline affects most long-term survivors. Cap omits skin findings, hepatic dysfunction and periodontitis (30-79%).

decisions.neurologic: involved: progressive neuropathy/neurodegeneration affects most long-term survivors; ocular albinism takes the third primary slot as a defining congenital hallmark.
decisions.ocular: primary: oculocutaneous albinism defines CHS; ocular albinism occurs in 8/9 and reduced visual acuity in 30-79%, establishing functional ocular disease.

basis: Inhaled Coccidioides establishes primary infection in the lungs; pneumonia is annotated 30-79%. CNS, skin and joint involvement are minority manifestations.

decisions.pulmonary: primary: lungs are the usual initial site of direct Coccidioides infection; pneumonia is annotated 30-79%, while disseminated sites are uncommon.

basis: Skeletal/CNS malformations define AFND; cleft palate 80-99% and hypopituitarism 2/3. Cap omits ocular findings (myopia 2/3, ptosis 5/8), nasal defects and nail changes (80-99%).

decisions.gastrointestinal: involved: median cleft palate occurs in 80-99%, establishing common structural oral involvement alongside the defining skeletal and CNS malformations.
